topline.text: A quiet start to the week — nothing new broke over the weekend across DfE, SEND, Ofsted, safeguarding or funding beyond what Friday's weekly issue already covered (the NEU ballot pause, the West Sussex DSG deficit, the closed SEND consultations).
The PE and sport premium digital expenditure return is due by 5pm this Wednesday, 30 September — flagged in Friday's issue, now just two days out.
topline.action: Worth a quick check with whoever holds the PE premium budget that the return has actually gone in.

diary.text: 5pm deadline for schools' PE and sport premium digital expenditure reporting return.
NEU national executive reconvenes to decide whether and when to relaunch the paused strike ballot.

items.lede: PE and sport premium return closes Wednesday.
items.body: This term's digital expenditure reporting return for the 2025/26 PE and sport premium — shorter than previous years' forms — must be submitted by 5pm on Wednesday. It's a routine compliance deadline rather than a policy change, but an easy one to let slip in a busy week.
items.action: Confirm the return is in before Wednesday afternoon rather than after.

box.label: Jargon-buster - reduced timetable
box.intro: Coming up in Rotherham's still-unpublished Schools Forum papers, and a term worth having ready.
box.text: A 'reduced' or 'part-time' timetable is a temporary, formally agreed cut to a pupil's school hours — usually while additional SEND or behaviour support is arranged. It should never be used as an informal way to manage a difficult pupil out of full-time education, and DfE guidance expects it to be time-limited, reviewed regularly, and recorded with parental agreement.
